turns.text: Welcome to the team. Today we'll walk through onboarding, starting with your equipment and account setup.
Great, I already have my laptop, but I haven't been able to log into the internal engineering wiki yet.
I'll get IT to grant you access to the wiki right after this call. It has all our engineering guidelines and architecture docs.
Perfect. Can you also tell me about the benefits package, especially the health insurance options?
Sure, we offer two health insurance plans, a standard plan with no premium and a premium plan with lower deductibles for a monthly fee.
How do I choose between the two plans, and is there a deadline to enroll?
You have thirty days from your start date to enroll, and HR will send you a comparison sheet showing the coverage differences.
Let's also cover the on call rotation, since your team participates in production support.
I saw that mentioned in the offer letter. How often would I be on call?
Engineers rotate on call roughly once every six weeks, for a full week at a time, with a senior engineer as backup.
That sounds manageable. What's the typical severity of incidents I might get paged for?
Most pages are low severity, like a slow batch job, but occasionally you'll get paged for something customer facing that needs quick attention.
One more important thing, our code review process. Every pull request needs at least one approval before merging.
Is there a preferred size for pull requests, or is that left up to the individual engineer?
We generally recommend keeping pull requests small enough to review in under twenty minutes, since large diffs tend to get less thorough review.
That's good guidance, thank you. I think I have a much clearer picture of my first few weeks now.
Great, feel free to message me anytime this week if anything about benefits, on call, or the wiki access is unclear.
